lines.trans: Hey! We have nothing to do with this—get out!
Could you please stop doing that?!
Hey, isn't there anything around here we can turn into cash?
Damn you—keep your hands off the women!
Are your parents still alive? If they are, call them down here right this second.
Damn it, knock it off!
You are taking over Muranishi's debt—every single one of you.
We have no choice. Muranishi sold you guys out and skipped town, so we're in a bind too.
Two billion in total—make sure you pay every yen back.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

meanings.en: bring to a halt; shut off
meanings.note: Transitive verb for stopping a car, engine, or machine.

examples.text: ここに車を止めてください。
エンジンを止めました。

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: open a store; bring out; hand in
meanings.note: 店を出す means opening a branch; 出しやがって attaches tough-guy disdainful やがる.

examples.text: 駅前に新しい店を出します。
examples.trans: We open a new branch in front of the station.

examples.text: 書類を出してください。

meanings.note: Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

meanings.note: Adverb.

examples.text: まだ終わっていません。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').

meanings.en: to stop; to quit; to give up
meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.text: 娘の体担保にして借金してんのか？あんなの親じゃねえって。
examples.trans: Borrowing money using her own daughter's body as collateral? That's no parent.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 村西の借金の肩代わりだ、お前ら全員でな。
examples.trans: You are taking over Muranishi's debt—every single one of you.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).

examples.text: ここで働いてるのは全員外国人なんだよ。
examples.trans: Everyone working in this place is a foreign laborer.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: て-form 売って links 'sell' into the next action.

examples.text: まだ羽があるなら、ほら、逃げてみろよ。空へ飛んでけ！
examples.trans: If you've still got wings, go on, try escaping. Fly off into the sky!
Are we really flying up into the sky?

examples.text: 当たり前だろ。こいつで真珠湾の上を飛ぶ。
examples.trans: Of course we are. We're flying over Pearl Harbor in this.

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

困る.gloss: be troubled; be in a bind

meanings.en: to be troubled; to be in a bind; to have difficulty
meanings.note: Godan verb.

examples.trans: That puts me in a bind.

examples.text: お金がなくて困っている。
examples.trans: I'm in trouble because I have no money.

meanings.note: With で (全部で), means 'in total' or 'altogether'.

examples.text: 地球局だって二十億で買ったんだぞ！これで契約させないのは不当だろ！
examples.trans: I even bought an earth station for two billion yen! Refusing to sign me after that is unjust!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Reassures that rules or steps are followed properly.

examples.text: ちゃんと確認しました。
ちゃんと並んでいます。

meanings.note: Godan transitive verb.

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Special reading きょう.
Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Everyday reading あした; pairs with また in また明日 ('see you tomorrow').
Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.
Godan verb; 持ってくる means 'bring'.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
